thread:
tess: Idea: replace big capacity plans with a small "lease redeem" flow. operator mints short-lived lease tokens (units + safety_flags), runtime redeems units as it serves. keeps operator simpler and lets runtime pick model variants.
omar: Curious about failure modes: what if operator leader restarts and ledger is out of sync?
priya: We require server-side dedupe and idempotent receipts. redeem(token_id, delta, trace_id) -> returns accepted_delta + remaining. operator must persist ledger before ack.
kevin: Add a grace_ttl so operator can mark token draining but still honor tiny inflight consumption. avoids mid-request preemptions.
ops-bot: Alert: recent autoscaler spike caused 3 tenants to hit fallback-to-quant when cost hints changed mid-request. See incident 6876500001.
tess: Good datapoint. safety_flags must be immutable on a token (e.g., "no-quant", "min-recall:0.9"). runtime rejects if incoming token flags differ from expectations.
priya: Proto sketch I'll draft: id, units, expires_at, grace_ttl, safety_flags[], preferred_family. Also explicit error codes: TOKEN_EXPIRED, INSUFFICIENT_UNITS, VIOLATES_SAFETY, SERVER_ERROR.
omar: Observability: runtime should emit per-token metrics (units_by_variant, fallback_reason) so console can reconcile billing and regressions.
kevin: Rollout plan: advisory tokens first, enable strict enforcement for a small canary, monitor dashboards.
tess: I'll schedule an RFC follow-up and assign owners. meeting 10:30 tomorrow?
priya: Works for me.
ops-bot: Note: monitoring shows 9% of dedicated pools had <20s headroom in last 24h.
